structured.reason: The description contains hedging language that the criterion explicitly treats as negative. Offending phrases: "Massaging it into your scalp can help condition hair and support its strength" (hedge "can help"), "Its antioxidant content may also make it a useful part of a hair care routine" (hedge "may"), and "Consistent use can leave your hair feeling conditioned and looking healthier" (hedge "can," which implies results depend on conditions). Under the strict standard, any hedge about how the product performs is a failure. Other wording, such as "Many people also use it to soothe chapped lips, diaper rash, and dry skin," is neutral to positive and does not cause the failure on its own.
